summary_of_change:
In contrast to market distress narratives, Zillow's operational performance across the trailing four quarters demonstrates resilient top-line expansion and structural share gains within the housing ecosystem. Consolidated revenue grew 18% year-over-year in Q2 2026 to $772.0M, supporting a real-time annualized run-rate of $3,088.0M with gross margins holding firm at 73.0%. Counter-cyclical monetization has been led by the multifamily rentals segment, which expanded 31% year-over-year to $209.0M as contracted properties reached a record 79,000 buildings.

Simultaneously, Zillow's strategic evolution into an integrated transaction platform continues to scale. Residential segment revenue rose 7% year-over-year to $465.0M despite macro headwinds in home sales velocity, powered by Zillow Showcase capturing over 4.3% of new US residential listings and Enhanced Market transaction-share coverage surpassing 52% of total volume. Mortgage origination surged 95% year-over-year to $2.2B ($84.0M revenue), proving the cross-selling efficiency of Zillow Home Loans embedded directly within consumer touring flows.

From a financial and capital allocation standpoint, fixed operating expenses grew just 2% against high-teens revenue growth, demonstrating expanding underlying operating leverage. Operating cash flow totaled $211.0M across the first half of 2026 ($200.0M in Q1, $11.0M in Q2), while disciplined share repurchases funded entirely from liquid reserves have reduced diluted shares outstanding from 256M to 228M over the trailing twelve months.

market_pricing_in:
At $29.30 per share, Mr. Market is pricing Zillow Group as a structurally challenged portal whose core monetization model faces sustained regulatory and competitive obsolescence. The prevailing bear thesis fixates on the forced unwinding of Zillow's rental syndication exclusivity with Redfin under FTC settlement mandates, which requires Redfin to construct an independent competing multifamily marketplace by 2027. Concurrently, sell-side desks point to the nationwide roll-out of Google Local Services Ads for residential agents as an existential threat to Zillow's top-of-funnel lead generation dominance.

This negative sentiment is compounded by high mortgage rates depressing existing home sales, insider share sales exceeding $81 million, and reported negative normalized Owner Earnings of $-0.29 per share ($-66.0M) due to substantial stock-based compensation ($363.0M). Consequently, the market trades Zillow at 0.0x P/OE and a negative Owner Yield of -1.0%, effectively pricing the asset as if its mid-cycle cash generation power has been permanently impaired.

However, this pricing discounts Zillow's structural advantages: an 80% direct, un-monetized organic search traffic moat, robust 73.0% gross margins, rapid counter-cyclical expansion in multifamily rentals and purchase mortgages, and the accretive operational transition toward high-take-rate Enhanced Market transaction-share agreements.
why_it_might_be_right:
1. Starting Baseline: The company enters the audit period with negative trailing normalized Owner Earnings of $-0.29 per share ($-66.0M total after deducting $363.0M in stock-based compensation and $130.0M in capitalized software/maintenance CapEx) against net balance sheet cash of $+0.95 per share ($+217.0M total).

2. Forensic Business Headwinds: If Redfin's mandated 2027 rental marketplace re-entry triggers severe multi-family listing price wars, Google Local Services Ads successfully disintermediates top-of-funnel residential search traffic, and US existing home sales remain frozen below 4.0M units annualized, Zillow's pricing power and listing conversion rates would compress across both buyer and seller funnels.

3. Skeptic Unit Contraction: Monthly active unique users contract from 230M to 205M (-11%), contracted multifamily property count stalls and rolls over to 70,000 units under aggressive pricing pressure from CoStar/Apartments.com, and residential lead conversion declines, dragging consolidated annualized revenue down from $3,088.0M to $2,550.0M.

4. Reverse Operating Leverage & Cash Degradation: Fixed enterprise technology, platform maintenance, compliance, and marketing expenses remain sticky at ~$2,450.0M. After subtracting physical and capitalized software maintenance CapEx ($130.0M) and ongoing high stock-based compensation ($320.0M), normalized Owner Earnings deteriorates significantly to $-280.0M ($-1.25 per share).

5. Downside Risk Valuation Floor: In a distressed stagnation scenario where the core Premier Agent lead generation engine loses pricing leverage, the business is valued at a conservative distressed asset floor of 0.6x sales plus remaining net cash ($1.20 per share), establishing a downside bear floor target of $18.50 per share (representing ~37% downside from the current market price of $29.30).

what_if_it_keeps_going_that_way:
1. Starting Unit Baseline: Current operational volume units stand at 230M monthly unique users, 79,000 contracted multifamily properties, $2.2B quarterly mortgage origination volume ($8.8B annualized run-rate), and >52% Enhanced Market coverage. Monetization yields generate a real-time annualized revenue run-rate of $3,088.0M.

2. 3-Year Bottom-Up Unit Volume Extrapolation: Over the 3-year visible runway, monthly unique users expand modestly to 245M via direct organic traffic; contracted multifamily properties grow from 79,000 to 106,000 through PMS integrations; Enhanced Market coverage expands from >52% to 75%; and annualized mortgage origination volume scales from $8.8B to $15.5B via integrated digital pre-approvals.

3. Projected Year 3 Revenue (Units × Monetization): Multiplying projected Year 3 unit volumes by expanding transaction monetization yields results in: Residential revenue of $2,380.0M, Rentals revenue of $1,220.0M (106,000 properties × $11,509 annual ARPU), and Mortgages/Ancillary revenue of $600.0M, generating Projected Year 3 Total Revenue of $4,200.0M (a 10.8% bottom-up CAGR from the $3,088.0M base).

4. Cash Cost Structure & Projected Owner Earnings: Against $4,200.0M in revenue, Cost of Revenue at a 74.0% gross margin is $1,092.0M, delivering $3,108.0M in gross profit. Deducting cash operating expenses of $1,880.0M (Sales & Marketing: $850.0M, Tech & Development cash R&D: $650.0M, G&A: $380.0M) yields $1,228.0M in adjusted cash operating profit. Subtracting normalized stock-based compensation of $330.0M, maintenance CapEx and capitalized software of $160.0M, and cash taxes of $80.0M yields Projected Year 3 Total Owner Earnings of $658.0M (15.7% Owner Cash Margin, or $3.06 per share across 215.0M diluted shares).

5. Explicit 3-Year Balance Sheet & Capital Allocation Bridge: Starting Net Cash ($+217.0M) + Cumulative 3-Year Free Cash Flow ($+2,130.0M) - Cumulative Share Repurchases ($1,600.0M to retire 13.0M net shares) = Ending Year 3 Net Cash of $+747.0M ($+3.47 per share on 215.0M diluted shares).

6. Intrinsic Fair Value Target & Expected 3-Year Return: With Year 3 Owner Earnings compounding at g₃ = 24.1% YoY (exceeding the 15% Rapid Compounding threshold), the 2-Factor Exit Multiple Matrix for a Narrow Moat business dictates a multiple of 16.0x P/OE. Capitalized Year 3 Owner Earnings of $3.06 per share × 16.0x ($48.96) + Ending Net Cash of $3.47 per share yields an Expected Fair Value Target of $52.50 per share. Against today's market price of $29.30, this indicates a total return of +79.2% and an annualized 3-year return (IRR) of 21.5% per annum.

What the Market is Pricing In

At $29.30 per share, Mr. Market is pricing Zillow Group as a structurally challenged portal whose core monetization model faces sustained regulatory and competitive obsolescence. The prevailing bear thesis fixates on the forced unwinding of Zillow's rental syndication exclusivity with Redfin under FTC settlement mandates, which requires Redfin to construct an independent competing multifamily marketplace by 2027. This negative sentiment is compounded by high mortgage rates depressing existing home sales, insider share sales exceeding $81 million, and reported negative normalized Owner Earnings of \(-0.29 per share (\)-66.0M) due to substantial stock-based compensation ($363.0M). Consequently, the market trades Zillow at 0.0x P/OE and a negative Owner Yield of -1.0%, effectively pricing the asset as if its mid-cycle cash generation power has been permanently impaired.
